items.title: How to answer a Telugu reading passage (పఠన అవగాహన పద్ధతి)
items.body:
## The task (అంశం 4)

A **~250-word Telugu prose passage (గద్యభాగం)** is given with **five short-answer questions** — **10 marks**. You are being tested on *understanding*, not memory, so **every answer must come from the passage**.

## A 4-step method

1. **మొదటి పఠనం (first read)** — read the whole passage once for the గిస్ట్ (overall sense). Do not stop at hard words yet.
2. **ప్రశ్నలు చదవడం (read the questions)** — now read the five questions so you know what to look for.
3. **రెండో పఠనం (second read)** — read again, **underlining** the sentence that answers each question.
4. **సమాధాన రచన (write answers)** — answer **to the point, in complete Telugu sentences**, in your own words where asked.

## Question types you will meet

| రకం (type) | English | ఏం చేయాలి |
|---|---|---|
| కేంద్ర భావం | Main idea | State the one theme of the whole passage |
| అంతరార్థం | Inference | Conclude what is implied, not stated |
| సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం | Vocabulary-in-context | Meaning that fits the sentence |
| ప్రత్యక్ష సమాచారం | Factual recall | Report the stated fact exactly |
| ధోరణి / ఉద్దేశం | Tone / purpose | Judge the writer's attitude/intent |

**Golden rule:** never add your own opinion or outside information, and never copy the whole passage.
keyPoints: Comprehension = ~250-word Telugu passage + 5 short-answers, 10 marks (item 4); answers come only from the passage.
Method: read for gist → read the questions → re-read and underline answers → write concise, complete-sentence answers.
కేంద్ర భావం (main idea) = the single theme every sentence supports.
అంతరార్థం (inference) = a conclusion the passage implies but does not state.
సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం (vocabulary-in-context) = the meaning that fits the sentence, not any dictionary sense.
Never add personal opinion or outside facts; never copy the whole passage.
items.mnemonic: Read–Question–Re-read–Reply (4 R's) for any comprehension passage.
items.source: standard Telugu comprehension method (SSC standard); APPSC 07/2026 Telugu item 4

items.title: Vemana Satakam — verse elaboration (వేమన శతకం)
items.body:
## About Vemana

**వేమన (Vemana)** was a people's poet whose **ఆటవెలది (Ataveladi)** verses teach **worldly ethics (నీతి)** in simple **spoken Telugu**. Every verse ends with the makutam **విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ** ('O Vema, hear this, delight of the world').

## Sample verse + elaboration

> అల్పుడెపుడు పలుకు నాడంబరముగాను
> సజ్జనుండు పలుకు చల్లగాను
> కంచు మ్రోగినట్లు కనకంబు మ్రోగునా
> విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ

**ప్రతిపదార్థం (word sense):** అల్పుడు = mean person; ఆడంబరముగా = pompously; సజ్జనుడు = noble person; చల్లగా = calmly/softly; కంచు = bronze; కనకంబు = gold; మ్రోగునా = does it ring?

**భావం (purport):** A mean person boasts loudly, while a noble person speaks gently. Just as **bronze rings loudly but gold does not**, showiness is not a mark of greatness — **quiet worth outshines noisy display**.

## How to elaborate (అంశం 2, ~100 words, 20 marks)

1. Open with the **theme** in one line.
2. Give the **bhavam** (not word-by-word).
3. Add a **real-life example** and a **closing moral**.
keyPoints: Vemana wrote in the ఆటవెలది metre in simple spoken Telugu; makutam = విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ.
Verses teach నీతి (worldly ethics/morals).
Sample bhavam: bronze rings loud, gold does not — humility/quiet worth beats noisy show.
Elaboration (item 2) = expand the bhavam in ~100 words, any 2 of 3 verses, 20 marks.
Structure an elaboration: theme line → bhavam → example → moral.
items.mnemonic: Vemana = 'Vinuravema' + Ataveladi; Sumati = 'Sumati' + Kanda — pair the makutam with the metre.

items.title: Sumati Satakam — verse elaboration (సుమతీ శతకం)
items.body:
## About the Sumati Satakam

The **సుమతీ శతకం**, attributed to **బద్దెన (Baddena / Bhadra Bhupala)**, is a set of **కందపద్యాలు (Kanda verses)** giving **practical moral counsel**. Every verse ends with the makutam **సుమతీ** ('O wise one').

## Sample verse + elaboration

> ఉపకారికి నుపకారము
> విపరీతము గాదు సేయ వివరింపంగా
> అపకారికి నుపకారము
> నెపమెన్నక సేయువాడు నేర్పరి సుమతీ

**ప్రతిపదార్థం:** ఉపకారి = one who helps; ఉపకారము = a good turn; అపకారి = one who harms; నెపమెన్నక = without counting faults; నేర్పరి = the skilled/wise one.

**భావం (purport):** Repaying a helper with help is nothing special. The **truly wise person does good even to one who has harmed him**, without dwelling on the wrong done. It praises **magnanimity** — returning good for evil.

## Exam tip

Name the **poet, metre and makutam** in your opening line, then give the **bhavam** and a modern example (e.g. forgiving an opponent). Keep it ~100 words.
keyPoints: Sumati Satakam is attributed to Baddena and written in the కందపద్యం metre; makutam = సుమతీ.
It gives practical nीति (moral counsel) for daily conduct.
Sample bhavam: the wise repay even harm with good, without counting faults — magnanimity.
Open an elaboration by naming poet + metre + makutam, then expand the bhavam with an example.
'సుమతీ' means 'O wise/good-minded one' — the poet addresses the reader.

items.title: Main idea, inference & tone — telling them apart
items.body:
## Three skills that trip up beginners

**1. కేంద్ర భావం (Main idea).** The **one theme** the whole passage supports. Test each option: *does every sentence relate to it?* A true main idea is broad enough to cover the passage but not so broad it covers unrelated things.

**2. అంతరార్థం (Inference).** A conclusion the passage **implies but does not state**. Ask: *what must be true given these lines?* Reject any option that (a) contradicts the passage or (b) adds outside information.

**3. ధోరణి / ఉద్దేశం (Tone / purpose).** The writer's **attitude/intent**, read from word choice:

| Signal words | Tone / purpose |
|---|---|
| దయచేసి…, తగ్గించండి (please…, reduce) | విజ్ఞప్తి / persuasive appeal |
| ముప్పు, జాగ్రత్త (danger, beware) | హెచ్చరిక / cautionary |
| అభినందనీయం, గొప్ప (praiseworthy) | ప్రశంస / appreciative |
| ఇది జరిగింది, ఇవి గణాంకాలు (this happened, data) | సమాచారాత్మక / informative |

**Discrimination tip:** the main idea is *what* the passage says; the tone is *how/why* the writer says it.
keyPoints: Main idea = the one theme every sentence supports; test options against the whole passage.
Inference = implied conclusion; reject options that contradict or add outside facts.
Tone/purpose = the writer's attitude/intent, read from signal words.
Persuasive appeal uses 'please/should'; cautionary uses 'danger/beware'; informative just states facts.
Main idea = WHAT the passage says; tone = HOW/WHY it is said.

items.title: Vocabulary-in-context & synonyms in comprehension
items.body:
## Meaning from context (సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం)

Many Telugu words have **more than one sense**; the passage decides which one applies. Use the **surrounding clues**:

- 'కరువు వచ్చి పంటలు ఎండాయి' → **కరువు = drought/famine** (not 'festival').
- 'ఆయన మాట తీరు మధురం' → **తీరు = manner/style** (not 'shore').

**Method:** substitute each option into the sentence; keep the one that still makes sense.

## Handy synonyms (పర్యాయపదాలు)

| పదం | పర్యాయపదాలు (synonyms) | English |
|---|---|---|
| నీరు | జలం, ఉదకం, వారి, సలిలం | water |
| సూర్యుడు | రవి, భానుడు, ఆదిత్యుడు, భాస్కరుడు | sun |
| చెట్టు | వృక్షం, తరువు, మ్రాను, పాదపం | tree |
| ఇల్లు | గృహం, నివాసం, సదనం, గేహం | house |
| తల్లి | మాత, జనని, అమ్మ | mother |

Comprehension questions often ask a **synonym or the meaning** of a key word from the passage — knowing common pairs saves time.
keyPoints: Vocabulary-in-context: choose the sense that fits the sentence, using surrounding clues.
Method: substitute each option into the sentence and keep the one that makes sense.
నీరు = జలం/ఉదకం/వారి/సలిలం (water); సూర్యుడు = రవి/భానుడు/ఆదిత్యుడు (sun).
చెట్టు = వృక్షం/తరువు/మ్రాను (tree); ఇల్లు = గృహం/నివాసం/సదనం (house); తల్లి = మాత/జనని (mother).
Comprehension often asks a synonym/meaning of a passage word — learn common pairs.
